title: Interlayer Adhesion in 3D Printed Cementitious Materials: Influence of Open Time and Binder Composition for Scalable Construction
content: This study investigates the impact of open time and binder composition on interlayer adhesion in 3D printed cementitious materials. As additive manufacturing (AM) emerges as a transformative tool in construction, optimizing layer-to-layer bonding becomes critical for structural safety and scalability. We assess how the hydration heat and rheological behavior of various binders—including ordinary Portland cement (OPC), fly ash, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS)—interact with time intervals between layer depositions. Findings confirm that delayed deposition weakens adhesion, particularly under high hydration heat. Blended binders offer improved resilience due to moderated kinetics and extended workability. This work contributes to standardizing performance criteria for digital construction.
